newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia derivatives market to launch new products.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia derivatives market to launch new products.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange (KLOFFE) said on Tuesday it would launch new products in 1997, including stock index options, individual stock options and an Islamic index futures contract.

"We should be launching individual stock options around July 1997, while the index options should be launched before that, around April or May (1997)," said John Duggan, KLOFFE chief operating officer.
The one-year-old KLOFFE at present trades a futures contract based on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) Composite Index.
Duggan said KLOFFE was also looking to introduce an Islamic Index futures contract after the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) launched the underlying index.
"This product is likely to raise a huge amount of interest, and should be launched around three to six months after the index is launched," said Duggan.
KLSE said in September it would launch an Islamic share index which would comprise shares of Malaysian listed companies whose businesses are acceptable to Islamic principles.
Asked for the reason for the launch of the new products, Duggan said: "Brokers are very keen for us to introduce more products. We are seeing some very strong signals from them".
Between three and five individual stock options are likely to be launched initially, said Duggan.
"We will watch the market closely and wait before we launch any more contracts. We want to maintain the market's focus," he said. "If there's demand for more contracts, we will launch them".
Stock index options are options to buy or sell a theoretical portfolio of shares, representative of a stock market index. -- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230 8911)
